Normal-Cayley eigenvalue formula with multiplicity chi(1)^2 is standard; exact symbolic re-evaluation of all 60 eigenvalues confirms every Ramanujan inequality strictly (tightest d=12: (2+2*sqrt(5))^2-44=-20+8*sqrt(5)<0; d=27 lam*=3+2*sqrt(5) approx 7.472 vs RB approx 10.198). D*=12 correctly framed as attained minimum valency with audit-plan forcing-proof hope honestly retracted in favor of exact 12-vs-3 split. No essential inference or computation fails.

originality.rationale: Nearest substantive prior Hirano-Katata-Yamasaki arXiv:1503.04075 determines Ramanujan-guaranteeing valency bounds for normal Cayley subsets of Frobenius groups and all subsets of dihedral groups of order 2p, with trivial-estimate coincidence vs quadratic-polynomial exceptions. A5 is nonabelian simple, hence not Frobenius, so outside that theorem scope; it proves bounds for different groups, not A5 spectra or verdict table. Yamasaki arXiv:1611.09977 (generalized quaternion groups) and Lubotzky arXiv:1105.2389 (expander survey) likewise contain no A5 threshold or per-graph normal-Cayley verdict table, verified by fetching records. Live arXiv search for Ramanujan Cayley graphs + A5 returns zero results, confirming no recorded A5 classification. The A5 all-Ramanujan verdict with D*=12, exact spectra, and 12-vs-3 trivial-bound split is substantively new and not mechanically implied by Frobenius/dihedral/quaternion bounds or general LPS/Alon-Boppana background.
